page: Amazon Web Services m8g.large is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton architecture. The configuration includes 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The processor features 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache, alongside native support for AES cryptographic instructions. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. The instance includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and providing a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight stable single-core efficiency alongside expected constraints in multi-threaded execution. The instance delivers strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 14.17 GB/s and mid-range single-core Geekbench performance of 1805.0. However, multi-core capacity is bounded by the dual-core topology, registering 3232.0 in multi-core Geekbench and 3402.97 in multi-core stress-ng tests. Large-block uncached read memory bandwidth achieves an average 56.21 GB/s, while database operation benchmarks hit an average score of 2995.63. Workload-specific throughput includes 4.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 5.02 GB/s in static web serving.

From an architectural standpoint, m8g.large delivers high instruction efficiency per core with dedicated execution pipelines free from hyperthreading contention. Because storage is fully externalized and network bandwidth defaults to 1 Gbps, performance bottlenecks can arise in high-I/O or network-saturated scenarios. The server configuration is an effective match for lightweight web serving, application staging, CI/CD runners, containerized microservices, and small database workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.large is a general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Configured with 8.0 GB of memory, it maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio suitable for balanced workloads. The instance operates without local storage or GPU hardware, utilizing external storage volumes and offering a baseline network speed of 1 Gbps. Performance data reveals strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression and average Geekbench single-core execution, though aggregate multi-core throughput and cached memory metrics are constrained by the dual-core configuration. Database operations and text processing perform within mid-tier brackets, while Redis SET operations achieve 4.69 million ops/sec. This hardware profile provides a resource-efficient environment for containerized microservices, development clusters, small-scale web servers, and lightweight backend services.
